pillar_reactions.evidence: Volunteered the value proposition himself before it was presented: 'I like the kettlebells. I like using multiple muscle groups and it's very compounded and dynamic feeling rather than just sitting on a bench and lifting dumbbells. It's kind of boring to me.' The time framing landed hardest — 'definitely like the shortness of not having to spend two hours in a gym somewhere. 30 to 40 minutes sounds good' — and he built his own analogy for it around sheet-pan cooking: 'If I had to clean up for an hour after with all these ingredients, I wouldn't do it. So that's just like same with the gym.' He also tied the mobility protocols directly to his own complaint about tight hips.

Understood, agreed, no questions — 'No. Sounds pretty easy.' He was already running most of the protocol since April and said so: 'I've been on it since April, so it's not going to be hard for me, if I need to make changes to it.' The one substantive exchange was in the other direction, with him supplying the detail: 'I'm trying to hit 200 grams of protein a day, but realistically, if I skip a meal, might be between 150 and 200.' Nothing in the pillar was new to him, which is a value problem rather than a comprehension problem.

Agreed without pushback or elaboration — 'Yeah, sounds good' — and to the mid-pillar check 'Does that make sense?' answered only 'Yep. Yep.' What he engaged with was efficiency rather than accountability: asked for his thoughts he said 'I like efficiency... more so efficiency so that I can have more free time, so that I'm not having to work all the time.' The rep had pre-framed the pillar around his travel schedule, which fitted, but the prospect never asked how the check-ins work, never asked about the app, and never reacted to the coach's personal phone number — the detail that produced enthusiasm on other calls in this batch.

anchors.raw: It's still a little bit out of the budget that I was, that I kind of had in mind, which was around $500.
anchors.note: A pre-formed monthly number brought to the call, and he had also pre-allocated a lump — 'I had some money for this'. Neither figure was asked for before the price was named. The three-month tier financed at roughly $400 a month was engineered down to fit this anchor, and he still did not buy, which suggests the anchor was about the total rather than the instalment: 'it's still a good amount for three months investment.'

anchors.raw: we are using the third-party financing processor. It's Paiva. Have you heard about Klarna? Yeah, yeah, yeah. I have that. It's the same.
anchors.note: The prospect already holds a Klarna account, so the instrument was familiar and frictionless — which is exactly what makes it worth tracking. Introducing buy-now-pay-later re-anchors a $6,000 coaching programme as a monthly consumer purchase, and on the three-month tier the quoted instalments totalled roughly $4,800 against a $4,000 cash price. The cost of credit was never mentioned by either party.

anchors.raw: He's got two 25-pound kettlebells, so nothing crazy. I started following Trevor and a couple other creators just trying to learn how to use them.
anchors.competitor: Trevor's own free social content plus other creators
anchors.note: The strongest anchor on the call and it was never contested. He has borrowed equipment, free instruction from the same coach he is being asked to pay for, and 22 lb of results since April with no coach at all — 'just from dieting and walking, I got down.' Nothing in the presentation established what the paid programme adds over what he is already doing successfully for free.

anchors.raw: our company is doing very well right now. But all the money that we make goes back in... the valuation's great, but you can't take a valuation to the bank right now, so we all take very low salaries.
anchors.note: High net worth, low liquidity — the exact profile the stated ICP's income criterion mishandles. He passes 'makes good money' on any reasonable reading and fails the affordability test that criterion is meant to proxy for. The rep never asked whether the business could pay, which for a marketing-focused co-owner of a drinks brand is a live possibility.

unmet_demand.want: Keep running and sprinting alongside the kettlebell programme — 'if I still want to go for runs in the morning, is that okay, or is that going to kind of mess up the routine?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep declined to answer and deferred to the coach — 'that's for Trevor to assess' — while noting sprinting is heavy enough to conflict. Honest, but it leaves an ex-college sprinter with an unresolved question about whether the thing he actually enjoys survives the programme, and it is unresolved before the money decision rather than after.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that accounts for narcolepsy and for currently being off stimulant medication
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed by either party. He disclosed the diagnosis, the medication withdrawal and the nicotine substitution, and the entire response was an acknowledgement. Nobody established whether the coach has handled it, whether sleep attacks are a risk under load, or whether his neurologist should be consulted before starting.

unmet_demand.want: A payment structure spread over more than six months — 'I don't know if you guys have like a payment plan or something like where I could stretch it out more than six months'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no in-house instalment plan longer than a split. The rep said an internal split would be preferable and interest-free but did not build one, and routed to third-party credit instead, where the twelve-month option costs more than the cash price.

unmet_demand.want: A commitment shape that tolerates unpredictable month-to-month income from several side businesses
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is a fixed six-month commitment paid upfront or financed at a fixed monthly instalment. He has a stable low salary plus lumpy irregular income he explicitly cannot forecast, and wants his tax adviser involved before committing. Nothing in the offer flexes to that.

unmet_demand.want: A reason to pay when self-direction is already working — 22 lb lost since April with free content and borrowed kettlebells
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nobody built the case. Phases 4 and 5 did not run, so the failure mode of doing it alone was never established, and the presentation described mechanisms he is largely already using. The programme probably does solve his stated problem — structure and routine under travel — and that argument was never made against his actual alternative.
